Seminar Title:

Study on the development of Fluorite-Perovskite composite from defect-engineered CeO2 and LaFeO3 oxides for charge storage, O2 and H2 evolution reactions at room temperature

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Ceramic Engineering

Speaker Name:

Subhadip Das ( Rollno : 518cr1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room, Ceramic Engineering Department

Date and Time:

07 Jul 2026 11:00 AM

Contact:

Swadesh Kumar Pratihar

Abstract:

As a burgeoning field of research, a stable, low-cost material with multiple active sites is of great importance for charge storage, water electrolysis, and green H2 production at ambient temperature. This dissertation describes an innovative and effective strategy for designing a sustainable composite that predominantly stores charge through a Faradaic reaction and involves O2 and H2 evolution reactions at room temperature. To attain this, cerium oxide (CeO2) and lanthanum ferrite (LaFeO3) have been chosen as the main constituents of the composite. The inherent stability of fluorite-structured CeO2 and the catalytic activity of perovskite-structured LaFeO3 are deliberately exploited for material design. However, before using them for composite construction, CeO2 and LaFeO3 are separately doped with rare-earth cations (Gd3+ and Sm3+) and alkaline-earth cations (Ca2+ and Sr2+), respectively, to improve activity while maintaining adequate stability. The individual doped/ undoped fluorite and perovskite materials were synthesized by the sol-gel auto-combustion (SGAC) route. For composites, an efficient, scalable, and convenient one-pot, one-step SGAC route was employed. In the comparative study of fluorite structured doped/ undoped ceria (CeO2 CE, Ce0.9Gd0.1O2 CGO, and Ce0.9Sm0.1O2 CSO), a threefold improved current density was observed for the cathodic part. Specific capacitance (Csp) of the materials increased in the order of CE &lt&lt CSO &lt CGO. The highest Csp of 345.16 F/gm was obtained at a 5 mV/sec scan rate for the CGO. Nonetheless, improvements in OER and HER activity parameters followed a similar trend to Csp. While for doped/ undoped perovskite ferrites (LaFeO3 LF, La0.6Ca0.4FeO3 LCF, and La0.6Sr0.4FeO3 LSF), both the specific capacitance and electrocatalytic OER-HER activity enhanced as LF &lt LCF&lt &nbsp&nbspLSF. Among all, LSF revealed the highest specific capacitance. Also, the OER and HER current density (50 and 7 mA/cm2), onset potential (1.68 and -0.229 V), and overpotential (490 and 400 at 10 and 7 mA/cm2) reached the lowest for LSF. The optimized CGO and LSF were then taken in different 10:90 (CL19), 30:70 (CL37), 50:50 (CL55), 70:30 (CL73), and 90:10 (CL91) weight% for composite formulation. The high Csp of 485 F/gm was obtained with composite CL91 at 5 mV/s. The remarkable HER activity (with the lowest overpotential of 398 mV at 10 mA/cm2 and a Tafel slope of 86.21 mV/dec.) and improved OER activity revealed that only 10 wt% of the LSF phase is sufficient to significantly improve the charge storage efficiency and gas evolution reaction properties of the composites. The 14 hours of OER-HER test and post-mortem analysis of the catalyst revealed appreciably stable performance, with superior retention of the defect structure and initial electrochemical (Csp, OER, and HER) activity.
